_comment: THE SHARED BANNED VOCABULARY. Read by BOTH guards, so neither can gain a term the other lacks. NoPersonalIdentityTests.swift reads it and applies word boundary matching to .swift and .md files. scripts/oss-scan.py reads it and applies the same word boundaries to EVERY file type in the publishing set. Neither guard carries its own copy any more. Everything here is already public: it ships inside the test that reads it. The never publish values live outside every repository and are python only.

allowed_contexts_why.com.gruxai.grux: The shipping bundle id. Changing it revokes every macOS TCC permission grant the app holds.
allowed_contexts_why.gruxai.com: The product domain. Product identity, not personal identity.
allowed_contexts_why.github.com/dotcomjack/: The repository's own URL. Every clone command, issue template link and advisory link has to name the account the project is hosted under, and a guard that fails on the project's own address makes documentation impossible to write.
allowed_contexts_why.@dotcomjack/: The npm scope the launcher publishes under. npm rejects the bare name `grux` through its typosquatting filter, so the scope is not a preference and the install command a reader types is `npx @dotcomjack/grux`. Same class as the repository URL.
allowed_contexts_why.Copyright (c) 2026 DotcomJack: The licence attribution. DotcomJack is the sanctioned PUBLIC builder alias.
allowed_contexts_why.\"author\": \"DotcomJack\": The npm package author field. Same public alias.
The old bundle id prefix. It survives ONLY in KeychainServiceMigrator and its tests, whose whole job is to hold the names an install may still be storing credentials under, and in private mini-services that never ship. Nothing user-facing carries it: the Mac app moved to com.gruxai.grux in August and the phone followed on 2026-09-22.
allowed_contexts_why.dotcomjack/tap/: The Homebrew tap, `brew install --cask dotcomjack/tap/grux`. Same class as github.com/dotcomjack/ and @dotcomjack/: a published package-registry namespace, which is project identity a stranger has to type, not a personal detail. Homebrew derives the tap name from the GitHub org, so this string is not a choice that could have been made differently.
allowed_contexts_why.bundleIdPrefix: com.gruxai: The prefix declared in the iOS project file, where it has no trailing dot. `com.gruxai` since the phone was renamed on 2026-09-22.
allowed_contexts_why.dotcomjack-grux-: The tarball `npm pack` writes for the PUBLIC package `@dotcomjack/grux`: npm derives the filename from the scope, so it is the same published identity as @dotcomjack/ and dotcomjack/tap/, not a private detail. Recorded with the trailing hyphen so it matches the version-prefixed filename and nothing else. Added 2026-09-22, when the 3.0.0 release evidence quoted the real artifact name and turned this guard red on main.

banned_why.dcj: Word boundary matched, so it catches `DCJ Command` without catching `com.gruxai.grux`.
banned_why.mco: The bare brand ABBREVIATIONS. The first version of this list carried `motorcityorganics` but not `mco`, so `case .mco: return "MCO"` was invisible to the very guard written to catch it. An adversarial reviewer found that, not the guard.
banned_why.mac mini: The owner's hardware, referred to in user facing copy as `the Mini`. A stranger running a Linux box was once told their host was a Mac Mini.

holder_files_why: Files whose JOB is to hold this vocabulary, so they necessarily contain every term. A guard cannot check for a word without naming it. Kept to files a maintainer reads, never ordinary source. This list is deliberately tiny: the other two holders, scripts/oss-scan.py and tools/leak-gate.py, are excluded from publishing altogether rather than exempted, because unlike this file nothing at runtime needs to read them.
